title: Hallelujah
headline: Cohen's label wouldn't release Hallelujah. Then came a 15-page fax.
caption:
"Ironic and amusing." That's how Leonard Cohen described all the covers of 'Hallelujah' in 2009, given his record label refused to release it when he first wrote it.

It took other voices to make people listen. Columbia had told him "we know you are great, but don't know if you are any good." John Cale's 1991 cover, built from 15 faxed pages of lyrics, inspired Jeff Buckley's 1994 recording. Cohen's original didn't reach the Billboard Hot 100 until after his death in 2016.
